question_en: A hedge fund will commit $15 million to a short sale of an exchange-listed stock. The fund sells short the maximum number of shares allowable when the margin requirement is 0.4. The relevant information is shown in the table below: No interest is paid for the borrowed shares, but there is a short rebate on the sales proceeds. If the fund closes out the position in exactly 1 year, the total percentage return is closest to:
explanation_en: A short sale of a stock happens when the short seller borrows shares, sells them, and subsequently repurchases and returns them to the lender. A short sale is profitable if the repurchase price is lower than the sales price ("buy low, sell high" = "sell high, buy low"). The profit depends largely on the number of shares that are shorted. Borrowing shares represents leverage, so all short sales are margin transactions. The maximum number of shares that can be sold short is a function of the short seller's equity in the transaction. In addition to the difference between the sales and repurchase prices, the return on a short sale also depends on: the short rebate: interest earned by the short seller on the short sales proceeds and calculated as a function of the investment value and the broker’s deposit rate. dividends that are paid on the shares until they are repurchased, which the short seller must pay the lender. commissions and other trading costs subtracted from the proceeds (not a factor in this question). The calculations for all components of the short sale in this scenario are shown below: (Choice A) 8.3% would be the approximate return if the short rebate on the sales proceeds is not included. (Choice C) 26.7% would be the approximate return if the $1.25 million dividend is not subtracted from the fund's gains.

question_en: Which of the following financial intermediaries is least likely to provide liquidity to the markets they operate in?
explanation_en: Financial intermediaries offer various financial products and services that connect buyers and sellers in financial markets. Market participants who want to buy or sell securities can use the services of a broker or a dealer: Brokers facilitate client trades but do not trade with clients. Dealers serve as a counterparty and trade with clients. One measure of market liquidity refers to the ability of participants to buy or sell when they want to trade with low transaction costs at market prices. By serving as counterparties to client trades, especially when market conditions make finding willing counterparties more difficult, dealers provide liquidity to the market (Choice A). Brokers attempt only to find counterparties for client trades, which does not add liquidity to the market. (Choice C) Mortgage banks provide liquidity to the mortgage loan market by securitizing mortgage loans, which provides capital that mortgage banks can lend to other real property purchasers at lower rates. The combined effects of both types of activity add liquidity to the mortgage loan market.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: When a retail investor transacts with a broker-dealer in a well-developed financial market, the investor would most appropriately be concerned with:
explanation_en: Brokers vs. dealers Brokers and dealers serve a similar function as intermediaries in the financial markets since they both facilitate trading. Brokers serve as middlemen who find counterparties for their clients to place trades, but they do not trade directly with the clients. Dealers trade for their own accounts, so they act as counterparties to their clients. However, brokers often serve as dealers, and dealers frequently act as brokers; entities that serve in either capacity are known as broker-dealers. Clients who use a broker-dealer may be concerned with potential conflicts of interest posed by the dual role: Brokers have a responsibility to try to obtain the best price for a client, and dealers profit by obtaining the best price for themselves. Often a client does not know whether a broker-dealer is serving as a broker or as a dealer for a particular transaction. (Choice A) Since dealers act as counterparties, they provide liquidity for their clients to trade at low transaction costs. Liquidity is not an issue when transacting with a broker-dealer. (Choice C) One characteristic of a well-developed financial market is a regulatory structure that oversees and monitors the activities of participants, including brokers and dealers.

question_en: A broker concerned with executing a trade in a timely manner and with a high probability of execution would most appropriately use a(n):
explanation_en: A rights offering is a relatively easy way for companies to raise new equity capital: existing shareholders are awarded rights that entitle them to purchase additional shares at a predetermined price and in proportion to their existing holdings. The subscription price is almost always below the market price, resulting in potential for an immediate gain. From a shareholder's perspective, the advantages of a rights offering are that rights: are distributed to shareholders with no additional investment required, are often marketable to other investors as a form of short-term warrant, and provide the opportunity to purchase new shares at below-market prices. The most significant disadvantage is the dilutive effect of the offering, which forces shareholders to commit additional capital to maintain their proportional ownership. (Choice A) Rights are not purchased from the issuer. Rights are awarded proportionally based on existing holdings. (Choice B) Once awarded, rights can often be sold to other investors, but a rights offering does not afford the opportunity for investors to sell shares back to the company.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor believes in the long-term prospects of a volatile growth stock and buys shares at USD 40. If the investor wants to protect against potential losses, which of the following is the most appropriate market order?
explanation_en: Market and limit orders specify how an order should be filled. A market order instructs the intermediary (eg, broker) to immediately execute the trade at the current market price, while a limit order instructs the intermediary to obtain the most favorable price over time. Since market orders prioritize execution speed over price, they are likely to cause price concessions. Buyers typically buy at higher prices on buy market orders and sellers typically sell at lower prices on sell market orders as compared to limit orders. (Choice A) Market orders seek immediate execution, not the best price throughout the day. (Choice B) Market orders typically have a higher chance of executing than limit orders. The execution of limit orders hinges on the availability of securities that fit the investor's price specifications (eg, maximum buy price, minimum sell price).

question_en: A publicly listed company needs to raise equity capital. The company contacts existing institutional shareholders to gauge interest. Six mutual funds and two pension funds participate and buy all the shares offered. This offering is most likely a:
explanation_en: There are three categories of securities: equities, fixed-income, and pooled investments. Since bond futures are derivatives and not securities, bond futures could not be in a securities-only portfolio. Such portfolio constraints are included in an investment policy statement to restrict the actions of asset managers. (Choices B and C) Gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are pooled investments enabling small money amounts to be invested in liquid securities. Common stocks are equity securities representing ownership in a company with a right to share in its profits.

question_en:
A trader buys a company's stock on margin and sells it after one year, with the following relevant information:

|   |   |
|---|---|
| Shares purchased | 100 |
| Purchase price | $45 |
| Sale price | $60 |
| Dividend | $1 |
| Commission (per share, on both purchases and sales) | $0.05 |
| Margin requirement | 50% |

Ignoring interest costs, and assuming dividends were paid on the sale date, the return on the transaction is closest to:
explanation_en:
Traders often borrow money (ie, buy on margin) to finance an asset purchase. The margin loan is the borrowed amount, which is combined with the trader's own funds that provide equity. The position's leveraged return is the net profit (loss), expressed as a percentage of the initial outlay.

- Net profit (loss) is the change in price after accounting for dividends, interest, and transaction costs, including purchase commissions and sales commissions.
- The initial outlay consists of the trader's equity investment in the leveraged position, plus transaction costs (eg, commissions on the purchase).

Calculation:
Capital gains = Shares x (Sale price - Purchase price) = 100 x (60 - 45) = 1,500
+ Dividends = Shares x Dividend per share = 100 x 1 = 100
- Purchase commission = 100 x 0.05 = 5
- Sales commission = 100 x 0.05 = 5
Net profit = 1,590

Initial equity = Margin x Purchase amount = 0.50 x (100 x 45) = 2,250
+ Purchase commission = 100 x 0.05 = 5
Initial outlay = 2,255

Leveraged return = 1,590 / 2,255 = 71%

In this scenario, the margin is 50% since the trader pays half of the total investment. This results in a leverage ratio of 2, so the trader acquires a position worth twice the invested equity. The gain in the stock, divided by the initial outlay, results in a 71% leveraged return. This illustrates the power of leverage: if the trader had contributed the entire cost of the investment, the return would have been only 1,590 / 4,500 = 35.3% (Choice A).

(Choice B) A return of 67% results from excluding the dividend and transaction costs from the calculation.

Things to remember: An investor's return on a margin trade is the net profit (loss), expressed as a percentage of the investor's own initial outlay. Net profit (loss) is the investor's profit (loss) after accounting for dividends, interest, and transaction costs. The initial outlay is the investor's equity investment plus any commissions on the purchase.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Investors participating in a rights offering most likely have the opportunity to:
option_b: sell their shares back to the company.
option_c: buy new shares below the market price.
explanation_en: A pooled investment vehicle (eg, a fund) contains a portfolio of securities and is owned by numerous investors. An investor benefits from the services of the portfolio manager and can purchase shares issued by the fund. Pooled investment vehicles can be open-end or closed-end funds. In an open-end fund (eg, a mutual fund), investors trade directly with the fund to buy or sell shares. Investors typically sell shares back to the fund at its net asset value (the fund's assets minus liabilities) per share. Funds typically issue and buy back shares daily. In a closed-end fund, investors cannot sell shares back to the fund (Choice A). If an investor buys newly-issued shares from a closed-end fund, the investor can sell these shares only to another investor in the secondary market. The investor typically sells these shares at a significant difference from the fund's net asset value (Choice C). The differences typically reflect market sentiments.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements concerning market orders is most accurate?
option_a: Market orders typically seek the best price throughout the day.
option_b: Market orders typically have a lower chance of executing than limit orders.
option_c: Market orders are more likely to cause price concessions than limit orders.
explanation_en: Primary market transactions occur when issuers sell securities directly to investors to raise capital. Primary market transactions typically include initial public offerings (IPOs), seasoned offerings, private placements, and shelf registrations for securities such as stocks or bonds. After issuance, the outstanding shares are traded in the secondary markets, where funds flow between traders and/or investors. In a private placement, companies sell securities directly to a small group of qualified investors; there are often cheaper issuance costs as less public disclosure is required. Seasoned offerings are sales of additional shares of a security that was previously issued. Although the company has already "gone public," these additional shares are new to the market. Therefore, this is a primary offering. Both a private placement and a seasoned offering are examples of primary market transactions (Choices A and B).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A bank allows employees to give investment advice without being registered. A market regulator investigating this matter is most likely concerned about:
explanation_en: Quote-driven markets are also called dealer, price-driven, and over-the-counter (OTC) markets. In quote-driven markets, dealers provide liquidity (ie, make markets) by standing ready to trade at their quoted prices. Most trades are between customers and dealers. Buyers must pay the price the dealer is willing to sell for (ie, ask or offer price), and sellers must accept the price the dealer is willing to buy at (ie, bid price). Almost all currency and bond trading as well as OTC stock trading occurs in quote-driven markets. (Choice B) In order-driven markets, customer buy and sell orders are matched based on price priority and time precedence. All automated trading systems and nearly all exchanges use order-driven systems. (Choice C) Brokered markets are those in which brokers search for willing counterparties on behalf of customers. Assets traded in brokered markets typically share several or all the following characteristics: expensive, unique, trade infrequently, and/or difficult to hold in inventory (eg, large blocks of stock, fine art masterpieces, real estate).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: .An investor has $12,000 cash to invest and wants to establish a short position on stock valued at $50. If the initial margin requirement is 60%, the maximum number of shares the investor can sell short is closest to:
explanation_en: Order-driven system: priority rules for filling limit orders The most aggressively priced orders (eg, highest-priced Highest priority: buys, lowest-priced sells) filled first Price Price takes priority over time and visibility Orders of fully visible size have priority over those of partially Next priority: or fully hidden size Visibility Visibility takes priority over time Next priority: Same-price orders filled based on time of receipt Time received Earliest received = Higher priority An order-driven system is used by nearly every stock exchange, with rules that match the buyers' and sellers' orders. Three basic rules determine how limit orders are executed ("filled"). The first rule is based on price. Orders with the most aggressive prices (eg, highest buy price, lowest sell price) receive the highest priority. If more than one order has the same price, priority is given to orders that are fully visible, meaning that the entire number of shares covered by the order is known. Orders in which the size is hidden, either fully or partially (ie, iceberg orders, have lower priority than fully visible orders. For orders with the same price and visibility, priority is based on when each order was received. The earliest-received order has the highest priority, followed by the second earliest, etc. In this case, Order 3 has the highest price, so it will be filled first even though it arrived last at the exchange. Orders 1 and 2 have the same price. Order 1 arrived first, but since it is an iceberg order, it drops behind Order 2 in priority. Order 1 receives only 100 shares; Orders 2 and 3 are filled entirely (Choices A and C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: If a fund's investment policy statement limits the fund to investing only in securities, which of the following is least likely to be in the fund's portfolio?
option_c: Common stock trading over the counter
explanation_en: Exchanges (and alternative trading systems) implement order-driven systems to match buy orders with sell orders based on price-related rules. As such, anonymous buyers and sellers provide liquidity to one another. In a quote-driven (ie, price- or dealer-driven) market, market participants trade with dealers directly; therefore, dealers provide liquidity (Choice A). In a brokered market, brokers arrange trades between willing buyers and sellers for unique instruments (eg, real estate, rare art) or large positions (Choice C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is least likely considered a primary market transaction?
option_a: A company issues common stock via an IPO.
option_b: A company issues common stock via a secondary offering.
option_c: A company repurchases its own outstanding common stock.
explanation_en: Companies use several methods to issue securities when raising equity capital. A rights offering is a relatively easy way for companies to raise new capital by tapping into their existing shareholder base. In a rights offering, existing shareholders are entitled to purchase, at a predetermined price, additional shares proportional to their existing holdings. In this scenario, the investor has the right to buy 1 share for every 10 shares owned. For shareholders, a disadvantage of a rights offering is that it is dilutive, forcing shareholders to commit additional capital to maintain their proportional ownership. However, there also are advantages for shareholders, including the following: Rights come at no cost. Rights are a form of short-term warrant that can often be sold to other investors. The subscription price is almost always below the market price, resulting in an immediate gain. (Choice B) In a private placement, restricted shares (ie, shares that can be sold only to qualified investors) are sold directly to a limited number of qualified investors. Participation in a private placement is not dependent on existing ownership. (Choice C) A preferred stock offering is typically issued through traditional public offering methods and offers preferred stock, not additional shares of common stock.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: The financial markets of a country are characterized by easy access to market information, low transaction costs, and fewer financial products than in most countries. This country's financial markets are best described as:
option_a: operationally efficient, informationally efficient, and complete.
option_b: operationally efficient, informationally efficient, but not complete.
option_c: informationally efficient and complete, but not operationally efficient.
explanation_en: Companies use many methods to issue securities when raising capital. In a private placement, shares are not offered to all potential investors as in a public offering. Instead, they are sold directly to a limited number of qualified investors. Private placements have several features that make them attractive to issuers, including reduced regulatory and disclosure requirements resulting in lower issuance costs than public offerings (Choices A and C). Privately placed issues are potentially riskier than securities sold through public offerings. This is due in part to reduced disclosure, which makes the securities more difficult to evaluate. Further, securities may be illiquid as they typically cannot be traded on organized exchanges until a specified time has elapsed. Due to the increased risk, private placements can be sold only to a limited number of wealthy, knowledgeable (ie, qualified) investors. Investors are compensated with higher expected returns (ie, lower offering prices) relative to public offerings.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A silver producer negotiates an agreement to deliver a specific amount of silver ore to a local ore processor for a specified price in six months. This arrangement is most appropriately done with which type of contract?
explanation_en: Traders often borrow money to finance portions of a purchase, a technique called buying on margin. The margin loan is the borrowed amount, and the equity is the trader's own capital. The leverage ratio measures the market value of the position relative to the trader's equity (ie, market value less any funds owed). In this scenario, the initial margin was 40%, so the trader borrowed 60%, or $24,000 of the of the $40,000 initial purchase. Subsequently, the position's market value increases to $52,000. After the trader repays the $24,000 loan plus $442 of interest, $27,558 of equity remains. This results in a leverage ratio of 1.89 (or 52,000 / 27,558). (Choice A) 1.85 results from not accounting for the accrued interest on the margin loan. (Choice C) 3.25 results from dividing the value of the position after the change in stock price by the initial value of equity. The stock's appreciation after the initial purchase increases the amount of equity in the position, which decreases the leverage ratio.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A risk manager is considering the difference between futures and forward contracts. Compared with futures contracts, forward contracts most likely:
explanation_en: Buyers and sellers send various order instructions to intermediaries (eg, brokers, exchanges) in connection with trades. Validity instructions state the allotted time frame in which an order may be filled. A day order to make a purchase, as in this case, is valid for the same day it is issued and expires at the end of that day if not filled. The client in this scenario does not specify any execution (ie, market or limit order) or clearing (ie, settlement) instructions (Choices B and C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A company will receive Singaporean dollars (SGD) in 45 days and immediately convert it to Australian dollars (AUD) on receipt. To hedge the currency risk, which of the following positions is most appropriate for this company?
option_a: Sell SGD at the spot rate 45 days from today.
option_b: Take a long position in the SGD forward today.
option_c: Take a short position in the SGD forward today.
explanation_en: Financial intermediaries such as brokers, dealers, banks, clearinghouses and exchanges help facilitate transactions that maintain a well- functioning financial system. The range of services may include connecting buyers with sellers, trading directly with clients, and providing facilities where transactions can take place. Dealers help clients fulfill orders by trading (buying or selling) with them directly. As such, dealers are traders who help provide liquidity. The profit that the dealer earns is the difference between the buying and selling price (ie, bid-ask spread). In contrast, brokers are agents who match buyers to sellers, either personally or through an electronic system (Choices A and B). The broker earns a commission for this service.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Of the following, the most likely distinction between an open-end fund and a closed-end fund is:
option_a: closed-end funds can be redeemed by the fund.
option_b: open-end funds are sold back to the fund by the investor.
option_c: closed-end funds usually trade at the fund's net asset value.
explanation_en: Dealers vs. arbitrageurs Provide liquidity by connecting market participants Dealers who arrive at the same market but at different times Provide liquidity by connecting market participants Arbitrageurs who arrive at different markets at the same time Dealers and arbitrageurs are financial intermediaries that often compete for trading opportunities since they both act as counterparties to buyers and sellers and provide market liquidity. Arbitrageurs provide market liquidity by simultaneously buying a security in one market (eg, domestically listed foreign stock) and selling the same security in another market (eg, foreign stock in its local market). (Choice A) Brokers do not provide market liquidity. Acting only as agents, they attempt to find willing counterparties for client trades. (Choice B) Dealers act as counterparties for both buyers and sellers in the same market but at different times.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A market's limit order book for a stock is listed below: If a buy limit order for 100 shares is entered and is said to "make the market," its limit price is most likely:
explanation_en: Gold is a commodity, and like other commodities, it can be purchased. A trader can create a long position by purchasing physical gold (eg, bullion) in the spot market, by buying a forward contract or by buying a standardized futures contract. As with most commodities, trading in the spot and forward markets entails costs and risks that are avoided by trading gold futures. Storage costs: Commodities are typically expensive to hold given the cost of storage and security, but futures positions can be offset by taking an opposite position to avoid delivery and storage costs. Transaction costs and risks: The quality of a commodity (eg, the purity of gold) can vary, creating risk, but standardized futures contracts specify such characteristics, removing those transaction risks. Counterparty risk: Buying the commodity or a forward contract is a bilateral trade that creates counterparty risk, but futures trade on an exchange with a clearinghouse that guarantees performance, resolving counterparty risk. Since futures contracts resolve these issues and minimize the costs of trading, they are more liquid than a long position in either the physical commodity or a forward contract. (Choice B) The arbitrage-free pricing of commodities such as gold versus gold futures insures their prices must track one another over time. Adjusted tor the cost of carry, price changes in physical gold and gold futures must be almost the same. (Choice C) Commodities futures exceed the price of bullion by the cost of holding bullion (ie, cost of carry), and holding costs increase with the holding period. Consequently, returns on long futures positions will be less than returns from owning bullion. After adjusting for the cost of holding bullion, the return on both positions is the same.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A trader buys a European call option on a stock for €2, with a strike price of €60, when the stock is trading at €58. Assuming no transaction costs, the trader should exercise the option only if, on the day of expiry, the price of the underlying stock is:
explanation_en: Quote-driven markets are over-the-counter (OTC) markets in which most trades occur between customers and dealers. In quote-driven markets, dealers provide liquidity (ie, make markets) by standing ready to trade at their quoted prices. Investors can buy or sell only at the price the dealer is willing to transact. Almost all currency and bond trading, as well as most spot commodity trading, occurs in quote-driven markets (ie, OTC). (Choice A) Brokered markets are those in which brokers search for willing counterparties on behalf of customers. Assets traded in brokered markets typically are expensive, unique, traded infrequently, and/or difficult to hold in inventory (eg, very large blocks of stock, fine art, real estate). (Choice B) In order-driven markets, buy and sell orders are matched based on price priority and time precedence. All automated trading systems and nearly all exchanges use order-driven systems.
